For a spin–½ particle the three Cartesian components of the intrinsic-angular-momentum operator are (in the z–basis)

Sx = (ħ/2) σx ,   Sy = (ħ/2) σy ,   Sz = (ħ/2) σz ,

with σx , σy , σz the Pauli matrices.  
In the question Ay is identified with the y–component,

Ay = c S ,  with  c = h/4π = ħ/2   and   S = σy =  [ 0  –i ; i  0 ] .

Hence

Ay = (ħ/2) σy =
           (ħ/2) [ 0  –i
                     i   0 ] .

1. Eigenvalues  
Det|Ay – λI| = 0  ⇒  (–λ)^2 – (ħ/2)^2 = 0  ⇒  λ = ± ħ/2 .  
These values are purely real; there is no imaginary part.

2. Eigenvectors  
λ = +ħ/2  →  (Ay – ħ/2 I) φ = 0  ⇒  φ+ ∝ ( 1 , i )ᵀ /√2  
λ = –ħ/2  →  (Ay + ħ/2 I) φ = 0  ⇒  φ– ∝ ( 1 , –i )ᵀ /√2 .

3. Commutation properties  
Sy commutes with the total-spin operator S², so its eigenvectors are also eigenvectors of S².  
Sy does not commute with Sz, and indeed the eigenvectors found above are not eigenvectors of Sz.

Assessing the statements:

(A) False – the matrix is written in the z-basis; its eigenvectors are not the basis vectors used to write Ay.

(B) False – the eigenvalues are ±ħ/2, entirely real.

(C) True – an eigenvector of Ay (i.e. of Sy) is automatically an eigenvector of A² (= S²), but it is not an eigenvector of Az (= Sz).

(D) False – as in (B), the eigenvalues are ±ħ/2; there is no imaginary part.

Therefore the only correct statement is (C).

Answer: C
